rationale.conceptual: An established but non-trivial DFT workflow: variable-cell relaxations under pressure, defect supercell modeling with fractional coordinates, and Kohn-Sham band-gap extraction. Requires knowledge of pseudopotential selection, convergence, and supercell setup, but no novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline (7 declared steps with dependencies, but core scored outputs from 3 CSV files): sequential geometry optimizations at multiple pressures, band-structure calculations, defect construction and relaxation, and data extraction. Moderate orchestration needed, but all within a single DFT package; no fragile multi-tool or large-scale data assembly.

difficulty.reasoning: Paper applies standard DFT (GGA, norm-conserving pseudopotentials) to compute lattice parameters and band gaps of forsterite under pressure and with hydrogen defects. Reproduction requires careful setting up of variable-cell optimizations, defect supercells, and band-structure extraction; not conceptually novel but demands solid understanding of plane-wave DFT. The pipeline involves multiple stages (geometry optimization → band structure) for multiple configurations, with moderate script orchestration.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small unit cell (forsterite), modest plane-wave cutoff (800 eV) and k-point mesh (3×3×3), no complex dataset; typical workstation-scale DFT calculation with a few GB RAM and negligible input data (structure files, pseudopotentials).
